node.title: Re: 5.24 -> 5.28 -- what has changed in autovivification?
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
I can't reproduce this, the output includes the "Can't vivify reference" error under both versions of Perl. Perhaps you're using different versions of the [mod://autovivification] module?

And what would be the proper way to check existence of value in last line in ver 5.28?

The proper core-only way to check in any version of Perl is exists $$h{a} && exists $$h{a}{x} && exists $$h{a}{x}{z}. Using [doc://exists] allows you to differentiate between a key not existing, a key existing and its value not being [doc://defined], and a key existing and having a [id://11104607|false value]. With no autovivification and if you know your values are always true, I guess you could say $$h{a} && $$h{a}{x} && $$h{a}{x}{z}, but I don't have much experience with that module.

Note that there are other modules you can use to look at data structures without autovivifying them, without changing the behavior of core Perl, such as [mod://Data::Diver].
